narrative: Thalbern is quicker than the beast. Before its eyes find him he has dropped behind a bank of brambles, hidden from it.

I loose an arrow at the owlbear's chest.
I put the kettle on and sit by the hearth, thinking it over.
I nod to Wollandora and ask her why she called me here.
I stop, hold my breath and listen hard to work out what is coming through the trees.
I think back on the elven tales I grew up with, trying to recall what the old songs say of these relics.
I stay flat in the bushes and search the bank and the woods for anyone else lurking out there.
I cast Detect Magic on the crate.
I cast Charm Person on Reinhard so he lowers his blade and hears me out.

action: I listen for what is moving out there in the dark.

I drop my bow and punch the owlbear square in the beak.

narrative: The owlbear has its head down in a deer carcass, tearing at it, its back to Thalbern. It has not noticed him.

narrative: The owlbear is on top of Thalbern, close enough to rake him.

narrative: Branka is bleeding from a deep cut across her arm.

I bar the door, eat a little, and sleep until morning.
I sit by the hearth for an hour, bind my cuts and catch my breath before I pack.
